name: pg_join_assume_distinct_implies
area: planner, DISTINCT ON and set-returning functions
goal:
The planner can incorrectly treat DISTINCT ON output as unique when a set-returning expression in the target list expands each selected row afterward. A join may then be removed or costed as unique even though the subquery produces duplicates.

Use a subquery such as `SELECT DISTINCT ON (id) id, generate_series(1,2) ... ORDER BY id` on the nullable side of a join. The outer query must preserve both rows generated for each id, and its plan must not rely on a false uniqueness proof. Plain DISTINCT, DISTINCT ON without delayed set-returning expressions, and genuinely unique subqueries must remain optimizable.
